headline: Heavy Sierra snow continues through Friday morning, with another 15–30 inches above 7,000 feet around Mammoth Lakes, snowfall rates of 2–3 inches an hour and ridgetop gusts over 100 mph, followed by a bitterly cold break and a weaker storm Saturday afternoon into Sunday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Around Mammoth Lakes and the rest of the Sierra, heavy snow continues Thursday, falling at 2–3 inches an hour this morning and afternoon and locally up to 4 inches an hour in heavier bands, with a 15–20% chance of thunder along the Sierra crest this afternoon; snow levels stay below 6,000 feet. By Friday morning expect another 15–30 inches above 7,000 feet (6–12 inches possible at the Mammoth airport) and 4–12 inches along US-395 in Mono County, with Winter Storm Warnings in the Sierra until 4 AM Friday. Ridgetop southwest gusts top 100 mph this morning, turning northwest at up to 50 mph this afternoon, and mountain travel will be treacherous. In the Reno–Carson–Minden area, steadier light snow from about 5 to 10 AM makes for a slick commute, with heavier bursts of snow (rain on the lowest valley floors) and possible lake-effect bands east of Lake Tahoe and Pyramid Lake this afternoon and evening; showers ease tonight.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Another round of showers Friday morning wraps up the storm, with valley floors getting up to 3 inches in total. Friday afternoon through Saturday morning is dry but very cold, offering a possible window for crossing the Sierra if roads improve (check Caltrans and NDOT), though melted snow will refreeze into icy roads Friday night, freezing fog may form in northeast California and Sierra valleys, and lows fall to the single digits and teens, with cold spots like Bodie, Bridgeport and Truckee possibly dipping below zero early Saturday. The next storm arrives Saturday afternoon with breezes and snow showers through Sunday, but it is much weaker: 3–6 inches along the Sierra crest and up to 3 inches above 6,000 feet.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Lingering cold air keeps snow levels at or below the valley floors with Sunday's storm, and a trace to 1 inch is possible for Reno and other western Nevada towns by Monday, though how much snow spills east of the Sierra is uncertain. The pattern stays unsettled heading into Thanksgiving week, with more storms likely to affect holiday travel, so check the latest forecast before any trip.

watch_for: Very heavy snow and extreme ridgetop winds around Mammoth Lakes and the Sierra through Friday morning
Icy roads, freezing fog and below-zero cold in spots Friday night into Saturday morning
Additional storms during Thanksgiving week that could disrupt holiday travel
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the heavy Sierra snow through Friday morning and the cold, dry break that follows, less certain how much of Sunday's snow reaches western Nevada, and expect more storms Thanksgiving week without firm details yet.
